Convert freguesia-level data between code vintages

Source: R/vintage.R
pt_recode.Rd

Portugal's freguesias were aggregated into "uniões de freguesias" in 2013 and partially de-aggregated in 2025; the maps before 2013 are finer still. This function converts freguesia-level data between four vintages: "2001" (the map the 2001 census used, 4241 freguesias), "2011" (the map the 2011 census used, 4260), "2013" (the uniões, 3092) and "2025" (the current map, 3259). The correspondence is derived from shared territory rather than stored, so any pair of vintages works; it handles the value semantics explicitly:

Usage

pt_recode(
  data,
  by = "dtmnfr",
  from,
  to = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  aggregate = NULL,
  split = c("error", "replicate", "weight"),
  weights = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame with freguesia-level rows.

by

Name of the column in data holding the freguesia codes (DTMNFR, zero-padding is repaired). Default "dtmnfr".

from

Which vintage the codes in data belong to (required): "2025" (the current map), "2013" (the uniões, in force 2013–2025), "2011" (the map the 2011 census used, in force 2004–2013) or "2001" (the map the 2001 census used). The 1991 census used an earlier map again, which geopt does not have.

to

Target vintage, one of the same four. Leave it out for the newest ("2025"); when from is already the newest, to must be given.

values

Character vector naming the numeric value columns to convert. Other columns are carried along: replicated on splits, kept on merges when constant within the group (otherwise set to NA). Columns called dtmnfr or freguesia are not carried: the result's own are the target vintage's.

aggregate

Function (or named list of functions, one per value column) used to combine values on merges, e.g. sum. Required when any merge occurs and values is non-empty.

split

How to distribute values on splits: "error" (default), "replicate", or "weight".

weights

For split = "weight": "area" (proportional to the area of the newest vintage's freguesias) or a named numeric vector keyed by the target dtmnfr (e.g. population).

quiet

Logical. Suppress informational warnings? Default FALSE.

Value

A data.frame with the target vintage's freguesia code (dtmnfr) and name (freguesia), followed by the carried and converted columns. The column names are the same whichever vintage you convert to, as in pt_lookup().

Details

  • finer → coarser (merges), e.g. 2025 → 2013, 2011 → 2025: freguesias collapse into a shared unit. Value columns must be aggregated, and only values for which aggregation is meaningful may be converted (raw counts can be summed; rates and medians cannot) — so aggregate is required whenever a merge occurs. If only some constituents of a target are present in data, the aggregate covers the present ones and a warning reports the partial groups.

  • coarser → finer (splits), e.g. 2013 → 2025, 2025 → 2011, 2001 → 2011 (22 freguesias created between the two censuses): a unit's value cannot be exactly disaggregated. You must opt in to a strategy: split = "replicate" copies the value to every constituent; split = "weight" distributes it proportionally to weights ("area", only when splitting towards the newest vintage, or a named vector keyed by the target dtmnfr, e.g. population). The default ("error") refuses.

Codes not present in the relevant crosswalk (including current freguesias created after 2011, which have no pre-2013 predecessor) convert to NA with a warning. For "2001", the codes the 2001 census areas use for Vale de Amoreira (090756) and Moita (100117) are accepted alongside INE's (090804, 101003).

See also

pt_crosswalk(), pt_registry, pt_join()

Examples

# 2013-era data onto the current map: sum-able counts, split by area
old <- data.frame(dtmnfr = c("010121", "010109"), cases = c(30, 10))
new <- pt_recode(old, from = "2013", values = "cases",
                 split = "weight", weights = "area")
get_map("freguesia", data = new, by = "dtmnfr")

# Current data backwards to 2013 units (counts: aggregate = sum). Conde and
# Gandarela (Guimarães) were one união from 2013 until 2025.
now <- data.frame(dtmnfr = c("030895", "030897"), n = c(12, 7))
pt_recode(now, from = "2025", to = "2013", values = "n", aggregate = sum)
#>   dtmnfr                                 freguesia  n
#> 1 030882 União das freguesias de Conde e Gandarela 19

# 2011-census freguesia counts onto the current map: many old freguesias
# merged into today's uniões, so aggregate = sum
old <- data.frame(dtmnfr = c("010101", "010102"), pop = c(500, 800))
pt_recode(old, from = "2011", to = "2025", values = "pop",
          aggregate = sum)
#>   dtmnfr       freguesia pop
#> 1 010128          Agadão 500
#> 2 010129 Aguada de Baixo 800

# a 2001-census rate onto the 2011 map: Agualva-Cacém became four
# freguesias, and a rate is copied to each
pt_recode(data.frame(dtmnfr = "111101", rate = 12.5), from = "2001",
          to = "2011", values = "rate", split = "replicate")
#>   dtmnfr   freguesia rate
#> 1 111118     Agualva 12.5
#> 2 111119       Cacém 12.5
#> 3 111120 Mira-Sintra 12.5
#> 4 111121  São Marcos 12.5
